$comment: Schema example for src/data/fees.json — the site's core fee ledger (798 fee items, 164 jurisdictions as of 2026-11-22). JSON has no comments, so the field documentation lives in 'field_guide' below. The 'example' records are real rows copied verbatim from fees.json (FI-320 and ALHAMBRA); they show the exact structure every data addition or edit must follow. This file is documentation, not data — never import it into the build, and never copy it over fees.json.

example.fee_name: Development impact fee - General City (per-dwelling base)
example.internal_notes: No direct official URL cited in the post; document named in source_note. The ~$18,798 worked ADU example from the post was rejected (computed, assumes 1,600 sq ft primary dwelling); this is the exact official per-dwelling base.
example.notes: Per-dwelling base for the General City area schedule. General City and Ontario Ranch are mutually exclusive area schedules — a parcel pays one, not both (Res. 2025-010; Ontario Ranch DIF schedule eff. 7/1/2026). ADUs of 750+ sq ft pay (ADU sq ft / primary sq ft) x base per Development Code Sec. 5.03.010.G.1 (Ord. 3296); ADUs under 750 sq ft pay $0. At the 1,600 sq ft default primary, an 800 sq ft ADU pays $18,798. For this rule, 'impact fee' covers only Mitigation Fee Act and Quimby Act fees (water/sewer connection charges excluded).

applies_to.rule: 'all' today. A district or area qualifier when a row covers only part of a jurisdiction.

area.rule: Area-schedule qualifier (e.g. 'General City' vs 'Ontario Ranch') when a jurisdiction has mutually exclusive schedules.

category.rule: One of: plan_check_permit, impact, school, water_sewer, utility_capacity, planning, construction_tax, permit.

confidence.rule: A | B | C. A verified row must have A, B or C — never null or empty.

dwelling_base.rule: True when the row is a per-dwelling base, not a per-sq-ft rate.

effective_date.rule: When the rate took effect. ISO ('2026-11-13') or human ('Jul 2026').

item_id.rule: Unique id. 'FI-###' for the original series, '<JURIS>-NEW-##' for later additions.

last_verified.rule: The date a human checked the source against the official document. ISO ('2026-11-16') or human ('19 Oct 2026'). Never in the future.

max_sqft.rule: Highest sq ft the row applies to.

method.rule: One of: flat, per_sqft, pct_valuation, valuation_step, valuation_table.

min_sqft.rule: Lowest sq ft the row applies to. 750 / 751 is the SB 1117 cliff line (impact fees: $0 at or under 750 sq ft).

notes.rule: Reader-facing note (SB 1117 effect, what is excluded).

rate_high.rule: Upper end of a range. Null for a single rate.

rate_low.rule: The rate. Null for valuation_table / valuation_step, where the rate lives in the table. Never negative. $0 is a legitimate value (exemption, shared connection, no such fee) — never treat $0 as an error.

source_note.rule: What the source says, in plain words: resolution or ordinance number, effective date, and the exact figure.

source_url.rule: External http(s) URL to the official document (.gov, city/county code, school-district or utility official document). Never an everylineitem.com URL (no self-citation). Never empty on a verified row.

status.rule: verified | to_verify | illustrative | conflict. Only 'verified' rows feed the published totals.

threshold.rule: Sq ft or valuation threshold the row applies from. May be a descriptive string (e.g. '800 sq ft ADU').

fee_schedule_url.rule: The jurisdiction's official fee schedule URL (external http(s)). Never an everylineitem.com URL. Two jurisdictions (LAKEWOOD, ONTARIO) still lack one — that is a known gap, not a pattern to copy.

post_slug.rule: City-series post slug, or null before the post is published.

primary_sqft_default.rule: Default primary-dwelling sq ft used by valuation formulas, or null.

source_note.rule: Note on the fee schedule source, when the URL alone does not say enough.

valuation_basis.rule: How the modeled valuation was derived, or null.

source.note: The field in this file is 'last_verified', not 'checked_date' — that is the name the pack's 'checked_date' refers to.
